function.mechanism: Insoluble TiO2 particles increase whiteness and opacity in foods through pigment/light-scattering effects.
common_food_categories: Soups, broths, sauces, and related savory categories

adi.basis: EFSA (2021) concluded a genotoxicity concern could not be ruled out and an ADI could not be established.

efsa.key_finding: Titanium dioxide (E171) can no longer be considered safe when used as a food additive; this informed subsequent EU withdrawal of food authorization.

adi.basis: ADI NOT LIMITED (not specified), reaffirmed at the 97th meeting (2023).

notable_bans: European Union: food-use authorization for E171 removed under Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/63, with transition tied to 7 February 2022 and 7 August 2022 market dates.

concerns.summary: EFSA could not rule out genotoxicity for TiO2 particles used as E171 and therefore did not establish an ADI.
IARC classifies titanium dioxide as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans), with monograph rationale noting inadequate human evidence and sufficient evidence in experimental animals.
Recent experimental studies report altered gut microbial composition/metabolism and inflammatory signaling after E171 exposure in model systems.
Recent organoid work shows ROS and DNA damage signals under in vitro exposure conditions, indicating unresolved mechanistic uncertainty.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA (2023) reaffirmed ADI not specified (not limited) for INS 171.
FDA continues to allow titanium dioxide as a color additive in foods under 21 CFR 73.575 with <=1% by weight condition.
A 2024 extended one-generation reproductive toxicity study in rats reported no reproductive/systemic/developmental neurotoxicity at tested levels.

adi_exceedance.notes: A classical ADI exceedance calculation is not possible under EFSA because no ADI was established; exposure meta-analysis reports up to 10.5 mg/kg bw/day and higher exposure in children.

risk_assessment.rationale: The additive is in the high tier because EFSA could not confirm safety and could not set an ADI, followed by EU withdrawal of food authorization, with continuing mechanistic concern signals in newer studies. FDA/JECFA disagreement lowers certainty but does not remove the high-risk regulatory signal.
key_factors: EFSA 2021 concluded E171 can no longer be considered safe
EFSA could not establish an ADI due unresolved genotoxicity concern
EU food authorization withdrawn via Regulation (EU) 2022/63
IARC Group 2B classification for titanium dioxide
Recent studies show microbiome, inflammatory, ROS/DNA-damage signals
